problem: The last sentence, 'This chapter shows how the load divides...', is a table-of-contents sentence, not teaching content; the instructions ask for no such filler.
fix: Delete the sentence and start the lead with the content: 'The load divides between nested springs in proportion to their rates, the solid heights must be checked so the springs do not clash, and the mean and alternating shear stress are compared with a torsional endurance limit.'

problem: 'At solid height the coils touch, deflection stops and the rate jumps' reads as if the rate of the set rises. Section 1 says the set rate falls to k1 when the inner spring goes solid, so a student can see a contradiction.
fix: Write: 'At solid height the coils of that spring touch and it can deflect no further, so that spring becomes rigid (its own rate effectively infinite) and the rate of the set falls to the rate of the spring still free.'

problem: The 1 mm gap is not specified as radial or diametral, and it is stated at free length only. Under load the outer spring grows in diameter and the inner shrinks, so the gap closes.
fix: Say: 'Keep a radial gap of about 1 mm or more on each side at the maximum load, because the outer spring grows and the inner spring shrinks as they compress.'

problem: δ_max = W_max/(k1 + k2) holds only while neither spring has gone solid; the bullet is stated as a general rule before the check that follows it.
fix: Write: 'If neither spring goes solid, δ_max = W_max/(k1 + k2). Then check each spring against its own solid load below.'

where: Section 3, first bullets and quiz Q6
problem: The fractions 0.22 S_ut and 0.35 S_ut are given without their life basis; they are values for steel spring wire at about 10^6 cycles and do not hold for other lives or materials.
fix: Add: 'These fractions apply to steel spring wire at about 10^6 cycles; other lives and materials need their own endurance data.'

problem: The phrase 'roughly 0.22–0.35 and 0.67 of S_ut' sits next to the mention of S_sy, so a student may take S_sy as 0.67 S_ut. S_sy is about 0.45 S_ut.
fix: Write: 'S_se is 0.22–0.35 S_ut and S_su is about 0.67 S_ut; if you use the Soderberg line, S_sy is about 0.45 S_ut, not 0.67 S_ut.'
